titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 1, second half
about: The second half of Spell 1 continues the speech that opens the long run of spells on the papyrus. Having spoken in the words of Thoth, the dead man now names himself a son of Busiris and lists the rites of Osiris in which he takes part, at Busiris, Rosetau, Letopolis, Heliopolis, Memphis and Herakleopolis, as priest and beside Horus. Three addresses, partly in red, then call on the gods who usher the souls of the dead into the house of Osiris, feed them and open the roads to it, asking that Ani may go in and out freely; the spell ends with the balance cleared of any case against him. This part runs from Plate 5, line 13, to Plate 6, line 44.

sentences.l: I · He-of-Busiris · son · of-He-of-Busiris
sentences.i: I am the one of Busiris, son of the one of Busiris.
sentences.n: The second half of the speech begins, still in black. ink 'I' is the pot, the basket k and the seated man, as in the first half. The name ḏdy is written twice: the ḏd-pillar doubled, two reeds y and a seated god. The pillar is the sign of Busiris, ḏdw (Djedu), and the second pillar repeats the first and is not read again. The reeds are the ending -y of a nisba, an adjective made from a noun: ḏdy 'he of Busiris' (Budge: Ṭeṭṭeṭi). sꜣ 'son' is the pintail duck with a stroke, and sꜣ ḏdy is a direct genitive. The god of Busiris is Osiris and his son is Horus: the speaker now takes the part of the son.

sentences.l: conceived-I · in · Busiris · born-I · in · Busiris
sentences.i: I was conceived in Busiris, I was born in Busiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes iw-w with a seated woman, then i-m with a seated man (Budge: āu àm-à); read iwr·i 'I was conceived', a passive sḏm·f like msy·i. The hartebeest iw (E9) with the chick w as complement and the woman as classifier is the verb iwr 'conceive' without its r; the reed i and the owl m before the man have no place in it and may be the following m written too soon. Budge's two groups are joined here as one word. The parallel msy·i m ḏdw makes the sense sure, but how the extra signs arose is not. msy·i 'I was born' is the three fox-skins ms with s as complement, two reeds for the weak ending, a woman giving birth (coded B3, approximate) and ·i: the passive sḏm·f of msi. ḏdw 'Busiris' is the doubled pillar with the hand d and the chick w as complements and the town sign. Busiris, in the Delta, was the chief city of Osiris in the north.

sentences.l: am-I · with · the-mourners · the-wailing-women · of-Osiris · in · the-Two-Banks(?) · of-Rekhtet(?)
sentences.i: I am with the mourners and the wailing women of Osiris in the Two Banks(?) of Rekhtet(?),
sentences.n: wn·i 'I am' is the hare wn with water n and ·i: the sḏm·f of wnn 'be'; 'I was' is as possible. ḥꜣyw 'the mourners' is doubtful: a papyrus stem with drooping buds (coded M16, ḥꜣ, from its shape), the vulture ꜣ, two reeds y, a bowed man (A16, approximate), a seated man and a stroke: a plural noun from ḥꜣi 'mourn', its w not written (Budge: ḥai). iꜣkbyt 'the wailing women' is i, ꜣ, the basket k, the foot b, two reeds and t, with a lock of hair (D3, doubtful), the classifier of mourning, and a seated woman. wsir follows without n: a direct genitive. Budge leaves the next group unread ('....'); it is divided here into two words, both doubtful. The first looks like the tongue of land iḏb (N21) over a canal, written twice: iḏbwy 'the Two Banks', a dual; Budge's footnote variants differ here. The second, two knotted cords (coded V1, approximate), t and the town sign, writes no r or ḫ; a footnote variant spells r-ḫ-t-t with the same cords, so it is read rḫtt, a place not identified (Budge: Reχtet). Wailing women, above all Isis and Nephthys, mourned Osiris in the rites of his death.

sentences.l: who-make-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: who make Osiris true of voice against his enemies.
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'who make true of voice' is the bolt s, the sickle mꜣ under the plinth mꜣꜥ (printed as one ligature), the oar ḫrw and the chick w; the arm ꜥ and the classifier of the first half are left out. It is taken as a participle referring to the mourners, its plural ending unwritten; it could also refer to the speaker. wsir r ḫftyw·f 'Osiris against his enemies' is written as in line 6 of the first half. The refrain of the first half returns: the dead man stands with those who cleared Osiris at his trial.

sentences.l: commanded(?) · it · Ra · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: Ra commanded(?) it: it is Thoth who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies.
sentences.n: Budge leaves the first group unread ('....'). It is a staff with a loop at its foot, the sign wḏ (coded V25, approximate), with a horned viper f joined to its top. It is read wḏ 'command' here, a sḏm·f, and the reading is doubtful: wḏ is usually completed by the cobra ḏ, and the viper may stand for it, or the group may be another word. st 'it' is the bolt s and t with plural strokes: the dependent pronoun, object of the verb. A pronoun object comes before a noun subject, so rꜥ 'Ra', the seated god with the sun on his head, follows it. ḏḥwty smꜣꜥ-ḫrw wsir then says what was commanded: a noun and a participle with no suffix, 'it is Thoth who makes Osiris true of voice', like 'I am Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice' in the first half. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw has the man with hand to mouth as classifier here, and wsir is written with the seat first. Ra, king of the gods, orders the trial.

morph.gloss: it, them (3rd person dependent pronoun, object of a verb)

sentences.l: commanded(?)-was-it · did · for-me · Thoth
sentences.i: It was commanded(?), and Thoth did it for me.
sentences.n: The same unread group as in the line before (viper and wḏ sign), with the same doubt. t and the chick w follow it after Budge's line numeral 18, and are joined to it here as one word: wḏ·tw 'it was commanded', with the tw of the passive sḏm·tw·f. Budge's group àri-nà (eye, water n, seated man) is divided in two: ir, the eye, 'did', and n·i 'for me', the preposition n with ·i. ir n·i ḏḥwty is a sḏm·f with the noun subject after the dative: 'Thoth did (it) for me'. The eye group could also be ir·n·i 'I did', the sḏm·n·f, but then ḏḥwty would stand outside the sentence. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes.

sentences.l: am-I · with · Horus · on-the-day · of-clothing · Teshtesh
sentences.i: I am with Horus on the day of clothing Teshtesh,
sentences.n: wn·i ḥnꜥ 'I am with', as in line 15. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon with a seated god. hrw 'on the day' (the courtyard h, the mouth r, the chick w, the sun and a stroke) stands as an adverb of time and governs the infinitive after it: 'the day of clothing'. ḥbs 'clothing' is the wick ḥ, the foot b, the bolt s and a tall fringed cloth (coded S28) as classifier. tštš is t and the pool š written twice, with the seated god: a name of Osiris (Budge: Teśteś), not explained here. Dressing the god's body is one of the rites of his burial, and the dead man takes part in it beside Horus.

sentences.l: opening · the-caverns · of · washing · the-Weary · of-heart
sentences.i: of opening the caverns(?) where the Weary-hearted is washed,
sentences.n: wn 'opening' is the hare wn and water n with a hatched door-leaf (O31) and a low sign printed like the sledge (U15) as classifiers: an infinitive, a second rite of that day. tpḥwt is t, the stool p, the wick ḥ, t and the chick w, with a house and plural strokes: the plural of tpḥt 'cavern, hollow', the word in the name tpḥt-f 'his cavern' in Spell 125; Budge renders 'storehouses', and which chambers are meant is not clear. n 'of'. iꜥw 'washing' is the reed i, the arm ꜥ, three ripples of water (N35A), the chick w, the low sign U15 and plural strokes: a noun of action from iꜥi 'wash'. wrd 'weary' is doubtful (Budge: urṭ): the swallow wr with r as complement, the hand d, a seated figure with hanging arms (coded A7, approximate), and a second swallow, which is not read. ib 'heart' is the heart with a stroke and the seated god. wrd-ib 'Weary of heart' is a name of the dead Osiris, here the one washed. Washing and clothing the body belong to the rites of embalming.

sentences.l: opening · the-door · of · the-hidden-things(?) · in · Rosetau
sentences.i: and of opening the door of the hidden things(?) in Rosetau.
sentences.n: sš 'opening' is the bolt s and the pool š, with a small cross (Z9) and the papyrus roll as classifiers: sš 'open, spread open', said of doors (Budge: 'unbolting'). rꜣ is the mouth with a stroke: 'mouth', and so 'opening, door'. n 'of'. The next word is doubtful: the bolt s, the pool š, two reeds y and t, with the roll and plural strokes (Budge: seśit). No word sšyt is known to this edition; it may stand for sštꜣ 'secret, mystery' (s with štꜣ 'hidden', the word of line 26) without its ꜣ. rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau' is the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, the drag-rope sṯꜣ (V2), a stroke, plural strokes and the desert-hill sign (N25). Rosetau is the realm of Sokar in the cemetery of Memphis, where the body of Osiris was said to lie hidden.

sentences.l: am-I · with · Horus · in · protecting · shoulder · that · left · of · Osiris · which-is-in · Sekhem
sentences.i: I am with Horus, guarding that left shoulder of Osiris which is in Sekhem.
sentences.n: m with an infinitive is 'in the act of': nḏ 'protect' is the sign nḏ (coded Aa27, approximate), then the pot nw, which is not read, and the low sign U15 as classifier. qꜥḥ is the hill-slope q, the arm ꜥ, the wick ḥ, a bent arm (D41), a stroke and a small sign coded F51 (flesh); it is read 'shoulder', and both the last sign and the exact sense (shoulder or arm) are doubtful (Budge: qāḥ). pwy 'that' (p, w, two reeds) follows its noun. iꜣby 'left' is doubtful too: its first sign is printed like the ankh (S34) where the chisel ꜣb (U23) is expected; with the foot b, two strokes y and the bent arm it gives ꜣby, the nisba iꜣby 'left' without its reed (Budge: àbi). imy 'which is in' is written as in the first half. sḫm 'Sekhem', Letopolis (Budge: Seχem), is the bolt s, the placenta ḫ, the sign m (Aa15), a bar with arrow-heads coded R22 (the emblem ḫm, approximate and doubtful) repeating ḫm, a house sign and the town sign. Cities of Egypt each claimed a part of the body of Osiris, which Seth had cut up and scattered.

morph.gloss: Sekhem (Letopolis), a city of Horus north of Memphis (place name; Budge: Seχem)

sentences.l: go-in-I · come-out-I · among · those-who-are-there · on-the-day · of-driving-away · the-rebels · in · Sekhem
sentences.i: I go in and come out among those who are there(?) on the day of driving away the rebels in Sekhem.
sentences.n: ꜥq·i 'I go in' (the bird ꜥq with q as complement) and pr·i 'I come out' (the house pr with r) are sḏm·f forms with walking legs and ·i; in pr·i a chick w after the legs is not read. m 'among'. imyw is the reed i, the crossed planks im, the owl m and the chick w with a seated god and a stroke: the plural of imy 'who is in', used as a noun, 'those who are there', the gods present. Budge reads ammu, 'the flames', which these signs do not give; the sense of the phrase is not sure. hrw 'on the day'. dr 'driving away' is the hand d and the mouth r with the low sign U15 as classifier of force. sbiw 'the rebels' (bolt s, foot b, reed i, chick w, a throw-stick, the kneeling enemy and a stroke) has Budge's line numeral 23 after its first sign. sḫm as in line 21, here with the owl m in place of Aa15, and as doubtful in its emblem. The rebels are Seth and his followers.

morph.gloss: Sekhem (Letopolis), a city of Horus north of Memphis (place name; Budge: Seχem)

sentences.l: am-I · with · Horus · on-the-day · of-the-festivals · of · Osiris
sentences.i: I am with Horus on the day of the festivals of Osiris,
sentences.n: wn·i ḥnꜥ ḥr hrw, as in line 18. ḥbw 'festivals' is the wick ḥ and the foot b with the festival sign (W3, a bowl on a hut), the sun and a stroke as classifiers. Its plural w is not written, but the genitive that follows, nw (the pot nw and a stroke), is the plural form and agrees with it. The festivals of Osiris were held through the year in his temples.

sentences.l: making · the-offerings(?) · on-the-day · of-the-sixth-day-feast · of-the-Denit-feast · in · Heliopolis
sentences.i: making the offerings(?) on the day of the sixth-day feast and of the Denit feast in Heliopolis.
sentences.n: ir 'making' is the eye alone: the infinitive of iri 'do, make', its t not written. ꜥbt is the arm ꜥ crossing the foot b, t, a lattice-like sign (coded Aa30, approximate), the roll and a stroke; Budge reads ābet 'the offerings', and a noun ꜥbt 'offering' fits the sense, but the reading is doubtful. Budge's three groups VI, ent and ḥeb are joined here as one word: the six strokes, water n, t and the festival sign with the sun write snwt, the sixth-day feast, the name of a day of the moon's month, not the number six. dnit after it is spelled the same way: d, n, i and t with a crescent moon (N11), the festival sign and the sun; it is another feast of the lunar month. The two names stand side by side without 'and'. iwnw 'Heliopolis' (pillar, pot nw, town sign) as in the first half. Days of the moon's month were days of offering for the gods and the dead.

sentences.l: I · the-wab-priest · in · Busiris · […] · who-is-in · the-house · of-Osiris · raising-up · the-earth
sentences.i: I am the wab-priest in Busiris, […] who is in the house of Osiris, raising up the earth(?).
sentences.n: wꜥb 'wab-priest, pure one' is water pouring from a vase over a foot (D60), a word-sign, with water (N35A) and a seated man as classifiers: the ordinary priest, who had to be pure to serve. The next word is not known: the mouth r and a recumbent lion (E23, rw) over a stroke, with the seated god. Read by their values the signs give rrw, or rw 'lion' with r as complement before it; Budge reads Rere and marks it with a query. The translation leaves a gap. imy pr wsir 'who is in the house of Osiris': pr is the house sign with a stroke. sqꜣ is the bolt s, the hill-slope q (Budge's numeral 26 stands after it), the vulture ꜣ and two reeds, which are not read, with a man raising both arms (A28), the roll, the seated god and a stroke: sqꜣ 'raise up, make high', the causative of qꜣi 'be high'. tꜣ 'the earth' is the strip of land with grains (N16), a word-sign. What rite 'raising up the earth' was is not known, and whether it describes the priest or the god is not clear; the reading is doubtful.

morph.gloss: wab-priest, 'pure one', a priest of the ordinary rank (noun)

sentences.l: I · seeing · the-secret-things · in · Rosetau · this
sentences.i: I am the one who sees the secret things in this Rosetau.
sentences.n: ink with a participle is 'I am the one who …'. mꜣꜣ 'see' is the eye joined to the sickle mꜣ with two vultures ꜣ, the first a complement; the eye is the classifier, printed first. štꜣw 'secret things' is the pool š, t, a small straight-sided cup (coded W10, approximate) that is not read, the vulture ꜣ, a small cross (Z9), the roll and a stroke: štꜣ 'hidden, secret' used as a plural noun, its w not written; the cup makes the reading doubtful in the print (Budge: śeta). rꜣ-sṯꜣw is written here with the drag-rope three times, for the plural of sṯꜣw. pn 'this' (stool p, water n) follows its noun. The secret things of Rosetau are the hidden body of Osiris-Sokar and its rites.

sentences.l: I · reading · the-ritual-book · of · the-Ba · in · Busiris
sentences.i: I am the one who reads the ritual book of the Ba in Busiris.
sentences.n: šd 'read out' is a waterskin (coded F30, approximate) with the hand d as complement and the man with hand to mouth: šd means 'take out' and also 'recite, read aloud' (Budge: seśeṭ, 'read'). ḥbt 'ritual book' is the wick ḥ, the foot b and t, with the festival sign and a tied band (V12) as classifiers: the book of the festival rites, read aloud by the lector priest. bꜣ 'the Ba' is the jabiru with a small bowl at its feet (coded R7), a stroke and the seated god. The Ba in Busiris is Osiris himself, in the form in which he can move and act.

sentences.l: I · the-sem-priest · as · one-belonging-to-him
sentences.i: I am the sem-priest, as his attendant(?).
sentences.n: sm 'sem-priest' is the folded cloth s and the owl m with a seated man. m 'as, in'. iry·f is the reed i, the mouth r and two strokes y, with a seated figure with a raised arm, the roll and a stroke, and ·f: iry 'one who belongs to', the nisba of r 'to', so 'his attendant' or 'his companion'. Budge renders 'his belongings'; with the man as classifier a person seems meant, but the sense is not sure. The sem-priest, in a leopard skin, led the rites at the tomb, acting as Horus does for his father.

morph.gloss: sem-priest, who led the rites at the tomb (noun)

sentences.l: I · great-one · of-directors · of-craftsmen · on-the-day · of-placing · the-Henu-bark · of-Sokar · upon · sledge-its(?)
sentences.i: I am the Greatest of the Directors of Craftsmen on the day of placing the Henu-bark of Sokar upon its sledge(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes rdit with the plain arm ꜥ (D36); read the giving arm di (D37): rdit 'placing', the infinitive of rdi. wr 'great' and ḫrp 'director' (the sceptre S42; plural not written) begin a title. The next sign, coded U23 (Budge: āb, 'the work'), is taken here for the similar drill ḥm (U24), which with the seated man gives ḥmwt 'craftsmen' and the title wr ḫrp ḥmwt 'Greatest of the Directors of Craftsmen', borne by the high priest of Ptah at Memphis; the reading of the sign is doubtful. ḥnw is the wick ḥ, water n, the pot nw and the chick w; a hoe-like sign (U6, approximate) after the wick is not read. skr 'Sokar' is s, k and r with a boat on a sledge (coded P3, approximate) as classifier. ḥnw skr is a direct genitive, Sokar's sacred boat. mꜥḫꜣyt·f is doubtful: the owl m, the arm ꜥ, a stalk with a curled top (coded M12, ḫꜣ, approximate), ꜣ, two reeds, t and a sledge (U15) as classifier, then t, w, ·f and a seated god, which are not explained; 'its sledge' follows the classifier. At the feast of Sokar the Henu-bark was set on its sledge and drawn round the walls of Memphis.

sentences.l: I · receiving · the-hoe · on-the-day · of-hacking-up · the-earth · in · Herakleopolis
sentences.i: I am the one who takes the hoe on the day of hacking up the earth in Herakleopolis.
sentences.n: šsp 'receive, take' is the sign šsp (O42) with p as complement and the low sign U15. ḫbꜣs 'hoe' is the placenta ḫ, the foot b, the vulture ꜣ, the bolt s and two reeds (not read), with a hoe (coded U6, approximate) and the low sign U15 after Budge's numeral 30; the reading is not sure (Budge: χebasi). ḫbs 'hacking up' is the same root with the hoe as classifier, and ḫbs tꜣ 'hacking up the earth' is the name of a feast at which the ground was broken. nni-nsw 'Herakleopolis' (Budge: Suten-ḥenen) puts the sedge nsw, with t and n, first out of respect for the king; a seated man (coded A2, approximate), n, n and the town sign follow. This ends the list of the god's feasts in the cities of Egypt, in each of which the speaker has a part.

sentences.l: O · who-usher-in · the-bas · effective · into · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: O you who usher the effective bas into the house of Osiris,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes stknyw bꜣw mnḫw m pr in red; i 'O' before them and wsir after them are black. The speech now turns to the gods of the house of Osiris. i is the reed and the man with hand to mouth: the vocative. stknyw is the bolt s, t, the basket k and water n, with two reeds y, walking legs and plural strokes: a plural participle of stkn 'bring near, usher in', the causative of tkn 'approach'. bꜣw 'bas' is the jabiru with the small bowl, a stroke, the seated god and a stroke. mnḫw 'effective, excellent' (Budge: 'perfected') is the gaming board mn, n, ḫ and w, with the chisel mnḫ (coded U22, approximate) and the roll after them: an adjective agreeing with bꜣw. m pr wsir: m after a verb of motion is 'into'; pr is the house with a stroke, and wsir has the throne first and no god sign. The ba is the dead person's power to move and take form.

sentences.l: may-usher-in-you · the-ba · excellent · of · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · with-you · into · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: may you usher the excellent ba of the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, with you into the house of Osiris.
sentences.n: stkn·tn is stkn with walking legs, then ·tn 'you' (t, water n and plural strokes), the plural suffix: a sḏm·f with the force of a wish. bꜣ 'ba' is written with the small bowl first. iqr 'excellent' is the reed i, the hill-slope q and the mouth r with the roll. wsir sš ꜣny 'the Osiris, the scribe Ani': the scribe's palette sš and Ani's name, with a seated man (coded A51) as classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw, the short writing: the epithet of the dead whose words were found true at the judgment. ḥnꜥ·tn 'with you'; r 'into'; pr wsir 'the house of Osiris'. The gods are asked to take the dead man's ba in with them.

sentences.l: may-hear-he · you · may-see-he · as · see-you · may-stand-he · as · stand-you · may-sit-he · as · sit-you
sentences.i: May he hear you(?); may he see as you see, stand as you stand, sit as you sit.
sentences.n: Four wishes in the sḏm·f, each with ·f 'he'. sḏm·f 'may he hear' is the ear sḏm (coded F21) with m as complement and the roll. After it the papyrus has only t, water n and plural strokes. As it stands this is ṯn, the dependent pronoun 'you', object of the verb: 'may he hear you'. Budge's footnote corrects the passage to sḏm·f mi sḏm·tn 'may he hear as you hear', the pattern of the three clauses that follow, which would mean the scribe left out mi sḏm. Both are possible; the translation keeps what stands and marks the doubt. mꜣꜣ·f 'may he see' (eye, sickle, two vultures; Budge's numeral 33 stands inside it), mi 'as, like' (a pot in a net, W19, with the reed), mꜣꜣ·tn 'you see'. ꜥḥꜥ 'stand' is the mast P6 with the arm ꜥ and walking legs. ḥms 'sit' is a bowl with a pointed rim, coded N41 (ḥm) as the nearest shape, with the bolt s and a squatting figure; the identification is doubtful. The dead man asks to move as freely as the gods do.

sentences.l: O · who-give · bread · beer · to · the-bas · effective · in · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: O you who give bread and beer to the effective bas in the house of Osiris,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this line in red as far as pr; wsir is black. ddyw 'who give' is two giving arms (D37, each d), two reeds y, the chick w and a stroke: the plural participle of rdi, which uses the stem dd. t 'bread' is t with an oval loaf crossed by lines (coded X4) and a conical loaf in a basket (coded X8), both approximate, and plural strokes; Budge reads tau, and the loaves make the reading doubtful. ḥnqt 'beer' is the beer jug (coded W22, approximate) with plural strokes, a word-sign. Bread and beer are paired without 'and', as usual. n bꜣw mnḫw m pr wsir as in line 30, here 'in' the house. Bread and beer stand for all the food the dead need.

sentences.l: give-you · bread · beer · at · the-two-seasons · to · the-ba · of · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · before · the-gods · all · of-Abydos · true-of-voice · with-you
sentences.i: give bread and beer at the two seasons to the ba of the Osiris Ani, true of voice before all the gods of Abydos, true of voice with you.
sentences.n: di·tn 'give' is the giving arm di with ·tn: a sḏm·f wish, 'may you give', or an imperative with ·tn added. t and ḥnqt as before. trwy 'the two seasons', morning and evening, is the plant tr (M6) with t and r before it as complements and a reed (not read) between, then the chick w and two strokes y, with two suns: the dual of tr 'time, season'. bꜣ is written here with a kneeling man (coded A2) as classifier. ḫr 'before, in the presence of' is the placenta ḫ and the mouth r. nṯrw nbw 'all the gods' is the god's flag three times and the basket nb with plural strokes. ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' (Budge: Àbṭu) is a single emblem, the fetish of the city on its pole (coded R17, approximate), with none of the signs that spell the name. Abydos, the city of Osiris's tomb, is the holiest place of his cult.

morph.gloss: time, season (noun; dual trwy 'the two times', morning and evening)
to, near, with; before (preposition; of persons)

sentences.l: O · who-open · the-way · who-open · the-roads · to · the-bas · effective · in · the-house · of · Osiris
sentences.i: O you who open the way and open the roads to the effective bas in the house of Osiris,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this line in red as far as n 'of'; wsir is black. wnyw 'who open' is the hare wn, water n, two reeds y and the chick w, with the door-leaf (O31) and the low sign U15 as classifiers: a plural participle of wn 'open'. wꜣt 'the way' is the road with shrubs (N31), t and a stroke. wpyw 'who open, who part' is the horns wp (F13) with p and w as complements, two reeds y, a small cross (Z9), walking legs and a stroke: a plural participle of wpi (Budge: àpui). mṯnw 'the roads' is doubtful (Budge: mātennu): the owl m joined to an arm (coded G17 + D36, approximate), t, water n, the pot nw and the chick w, with the road sign and plural strokes; it is read as the plural of mṯn 'road', with t written for ṯ and the arm not read. Opening the ways is the office of Wepwawet, 'Opener of the Ways', whose name uses the same verb and noun as wpyw … wꜣt.

sentences.l: open · then-you · for-him · the-way
sentences.i: Open, then, the way for him,
sentences.n: wn 'open' (hare, water n, door-leaf and U15) is now the imperative. irf·tn is the reed i, the mouth r and the viper f, with ·tn: irf 'then' is the particle made of r with ·f, and the plural suffix after it points it at the gods addressed, 'you, then' (Budge: àref-ten). It could also be read ir·tn, r with a suffix after an imperative, with the f added; the sense is the same. n·f 'for him' is water n and the viper. wꜣt 'the way'.

sentences.l: open · then-you · the-roads · to · the-ba · of · the-Osiris · the-scribe · accountant · of-the-god's-offerings · of-gods · all · Ani · with-you
sentences.i: open, then, the roads to the ba of the Osiris, the accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, with you.
sentences.n: wp 'open' is the horns wp with p and w as complements, the small cross and the roll: the imperative of wpi. irf·tn and mṯnw as before; Budge's numeral 39 stands before the road sign. wsir is written eye first. sš ḥsb, the palette sš and the sign ḥsb (coded Aa2, approximate) with the roll, is the title 'accounting scribe'. Budge's groups neter and ḥetepu are joined here as one word, ḥtp-nṯr 'god's offerings': the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, and the offering table ḥtp. The flag stands in square brackets in Budge's hieroglyphs: it is restored where the papyrus is damaged. nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods' follows as a direct genitive, and ꜣny closes the title without mꜣꜥ-ḫrw. Ani's title says he kept the accounts of the temple offerings.

sentences.l: may-go-in-he · with · […] · may-come-out-he · in · peace · from · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: May he go in with […] and come out in peace from the house of Osiris.
sentences.n: ꜥq·f 'may he go in' and pr·f 'may he come out' are sḏm·f wishes with ·f. m 'with'. The next word is the hand d, water n and the hand d again with a horned bull's head (coded F1, approximate): dnd. A word dnd 'rage' has this spelling, but rage does not suit the wish, and Budge's 'confidence' is a guess from the sense; the translation leaves a gap. m ḥtp 'in peace': ḥtp is the offering table, a word-sign, with t and p as complements and the roll. m 'from'. To go in and out of the world below at will is what the spells of going forth by day promise.

sentences.l: not · shall-be-repelled-he · not · shall-be-turned-back-he
sentences.i: He shall not be repelled, he shall not be turned back.
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms of negation (D35) with water n as complement, before the passive sḏm·tw·f. ḫsf 'repel' is the spindle with the horned viper joined to it (U35), a single sign, with the low sign U15; then t and w, the tw of the passive, and ·f. šnꜥ 'turn back' is the loop šn (V7) with n, the arm ꜥ and walking legs; a recumbent lion (E23) after the arm is not read (Budge: śenār, taking it for r). n with the sḏm·f mostly denies the past ('he was not repelled'); among the wishes it is taken as future, as nn would be: 'he shall not be repelled'. A wish is not denied with n. Guardians at the gates of the world below turn back the unworthy dead.

sentences.l: may-go-in-he · praised · may-come-out-he · loved · may-be-true-of-voice-he
sentences.i: May he go in praised and come out loved; may he be true of voice.
sentences.n: ḥsw 'praised' is the wick ḥ, the jar ḥs (W14), a tall narrow sign coded S29 for s (approximate), the chick w and the man with hand to mouth: the stative of ḥsi 'praise, favour', with the ending w, describing the subject. mrw 'loved' is the hoe mr with r and w and the same man: the stative of mri 'love'. Budge renders them 'as he pleaseth … as he desireth', which the stative endings do not support. pr·f has a chick w that is not read, as pr·i in line 22 (there after the legs). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw·f 'may he be true of voice' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ, the oar and w, the man with hand to mouth and ·f: the epithet used as a verb in the sḏm·f. To be praised and loved by the gods is the reward of the dead man found true.

sentences.l: may-be-done · commands-his · in · the-house · of-Osiris
sentences.i: May his commands be done in the house of Osiris.
sentences.n: ir·w 'may be done' is the eye with the chick w: the passive sḏm·f of iri, with the w it sometimes shows. wḏt·f 'his commands' is the wḏ sign (coded V24, approximate) with the hand d as complement, a second hand that is not read, t, the roll, a stroke and ·f: wḏt, the noun from wḏ 'command'. If a plural is meant, its w is not written. In the house of Osiris the dead man is to give orders, as a lord there.

morph.gloss: command, decree (noun f. wḏt, from the verb)

sentences.l: may-walk-he · may-speak-he · with-you · may-be-a-spirit-he · with-you
sentences.i: May he walk and speak with you; may he be a glorious spirit with you.
sentences.n: šm·f 'may he walk' is the pool with legs šm (N40) with m and walking legs, printed before Budge's numeral 43. ḏd·f 'may he speak' is the cobra ḏ and the hand d, then t, the man with hand to mouth, a stroke and ·f; the t is not read here, though it could make the word ḏdt·f 'his speech'. ꜣḫ·f 'may he be an ꜣḫ' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, the roll and ·f: the verb 'be glorious, effective', from which ꜣḫ 'spirit' comes. ḥnꜥ·tn 'with you', twice. The ꜣḫ is the dead made into an effective spirit of light.

morph.gloss: to be glorious, effective; to be an effective spirit (verb)

sentences.l: not · was-found · fault-his · there
sentences.i: No fault of his was found there.
sentences.n: n 'not', as before. gm·n·tw is the ibis gm (G28) with m as complement, water n of the sḏm·n·f, and t and w: the passive sḏm·n·tw·f of gmi 'find', with the noun subject after it. n with the sḏm·n·f is often 'cannot', so the clause may also be 'his fault cannot be found'. wn·f 'his fault' is the hare wn with n and the small bird of bad things (G37), and ·f; the hare, water and bird stand in square brackets in Budge's hieroglyphs, restored where the papyrus is damaged. This wn 'fault, failing' is a different word from wn 'open'. im 'there' (reed and owl): in the hall of judgment.

sentences.l: the-balance · is-emptied · of · case-his
sentences.i: The balance is cleared of his case.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes s-s-w with the bird of bad things; read sšw, with the second s standing for š, and the reading is doubtful (Budge: sesu-θà, 'have been emptied'). iw (reed and chick) opens the statement and is not translated. mḫꜣt 'balance' is doubtful in the print too (Budge: māχat): the owl m with an arm joined to it, as in mṯnw, not read; a post with a loop on top (coded U39) where the sign ḫꜣ is expected (cf. line 29); the vulture ꜣ, t, two strokes and the balance (U38) as classifier. sšw is the causative of šwi 'be empty', 'make empty', in the stative with its third feminine ending ·ṯi (V13 ṯ and the reed), agreeing with mḫꜣt: 'is emptied'. m 'of'. sp·f 'his case, his deed' is the bolt s and the stool p as complements, the threshing floor sp (O50) and ·f; the viper is in square brackets, Budge's restoration. Nothing is left in the scale against him. The spell ends here.

morph.gloss: she, it (3rd person feminine singular ending of the stative, written ·ṯi)
